page.description: Vanilla OS editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A desktop Linux distribution built as a simple, ready-to-use system: an immutable core with GNOME, applications installed in tuned containers, and the Apx package tool.
pros: Immutable base: a bad update rolls back instead of breaking the system.
GNOME desktop with a plain, guided first-run setup.
Apx installs Debian, Arch, Fedora or AUR packages in separate containers.
amd64 and arm64 images are published for every release.
cons: The container model is unfamiliar if you expect a classic package manager.
One desktop edition only: no minimal or server image.
Older releases are explicitly deprecated and receive no fixes.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Vanilla OS; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the ISO for your architecture to a USB stick and boot the live system, then run the installer. Writing erases the stick; the installer partitions or erases the target disk.
